title: List only prior stage reports that actually exist in stage prompts
goal: PROBLEM: Stage prompts include a Previous Reports section that can name files which do not exist in the task docs folder. Agents then waste effort attempting to read phantom files and must second-guess which history is real, slowing every downstream stage. FIX: When rendering the Previous Reports list, the engine must enumerate the files actually present under the task docs directory (docs/tasks/<taskId>/) and list only those; never emit stale, planned, or templated filenames. If a report referenced by stage history is missing from disk, either omit it or mark it explicitly as MISSING rather than presenting it as available. Acceptance: for any task, every file named in Previous Reports opens successfully from the workspace, and no manually-created report on disk is omitted. CASE STUDY: KainBain task 0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5 (settings-page overflow fix) — its retrospective prompt listed idea-20261115-222653.md, review-plan-20261115-223714.md, automated-tests-failure-20261115-233558.md and final-review-20261116-064824.md, none of which existed on disk (only SURVEY.md, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md, OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md and three verdict/review files were present); see docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/stage-review-20261116.md which flags the same discrepancy.

# Implementation Plan — Disk-authoritative "Previous Reports" in stage prompts

**Task:** 4f927ecb-ba3a-423c-ace3-5f7dd7d36896
**Problem:** Stage prompts render a `# Previous Reports` list from task/history metadata (`task.reports`) without checking the filesystem, so stages name files that do not exist under `docs/tasks/<taskId>/`. Agents waste effort reading phantom files (case study: task `0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5`, whose retrospective prompt listed `idea-20261115-222653.md`, `review-plan-20261115-223714.md`, `automated-tests-failure-20261115-233558.md`, `final-review-20261116-064824.md` — none on disk; flagged in `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/stage-review-20261116.md`).

**Fix (one sentence):** When rendering the Previous Reports list, enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` and list only those — never stale, planned, or templated filenames.

**Acceptance criteria:**
1. For any task, every file named in `# Previous Reports` opens successfully from the workspace.
2. No manually-created file on disk in the task docs folder is omitted from the listing (accounted for either by name or by an explicit overflow count + folder pointer — see survey q2 note).

---

## 1. Survey decisions to encode (from SURVEY.md, round 1)

| Q | Decision | Requirement |
|---|----------|-------------|
| q1 | "Leave it out completely" | A report referenced by history but missing on disk is **omitted** from the prompt list (no `MISSING` label in the prompt). |
| q2 | "Every file in the folder, including pictures", note: cap to ~top 5 most recently edited, then a guide to view the rest | Enumerate **all top-level files** in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` (any extension, not just `.md`; `task.md` itself excluded), newest first, capped at `N` (default 5) with an overflow line pointing at the folder. |
| q3 | "Newest first" | Sort by file mtime, descending (filename tiebreak). |
| q4 | "Keep the section but say that no reports are available yet" | Empty/missing task folder → the section still renders, with an explicit "no previous reports available yet" line. |
| q5 | "Every stage prompt of every task, always" | The rule lives at the single render choke point in `curatePrompt` / `interpolatePromptKeywords`, so all callers get it uniformly. |

The task statement allows "omit or mark MISSING"; the survey chose **omit** — implement omit.

---

## 2. Root cause (research findings)

The prompt list is rendered from **metadata only**, never reconciled with disk:

- `api/promptCuration.js:883-895` (`curatePrompt`, section 3) builds `# Previous Reports` from `options.previousReports || options.reports || task.reports` (`api/promptCuration.js:760-776`) and prints each entry verbatim.
- `api/promptCuration.js:348-358` (`interpolatePromptKeywords`, `{{previousReports}}`) merges `reports` + `latestReports` + `task.reports` — same phantom source. This keyword also feeds `KAINBAIN_REPORTS` for command stages (`api/flow/commandStages.js:526`), and `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` (`api/promptCuration.js:380-437`) derive from the same merged list.
- `task.reports` accumulates entries in `saveStageReport` (`api/watch/stageReports.js:247-257`) and in `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593-667`), which merges in-memory metadata with on-disk `.md` files but **never drops metadata entries whose file is gone** — phantom entries persist forever and flow into prompts.
- Callers that pass the list: `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js:693` (`store.getTaskReports(...)` → `reports` option), `api/flow/curateRunnerPrompt.js:48` (`task.reports`), plus the `task.reports` fallback for `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js:249,323` and `api/flow/taskFlowRoutes.js:60`.

Verified against the case study: `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/` contains only `SURVEY.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md`, three verdict/review `.md` files and three `.png`s — the four files named in the retrospective prompt do not exist.

---

## 3. Design (make the change easy, then make the change)

**Principle:** one disk-authoritative choke point at render time, so every caller and every task gets the fix without touching dispatch code.

1. **New enumerator** `listTaskDocsFiles(projectCwd, taskId, docsProject)` in a new module under `api/work/` (e.g. `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`):
   - Resolves the task docs dir via the existing `resolveTaskDocsDir(projectCwd, docsProject, taskId)` (`api/docsPath.js`) so custom `docsDirName` projects work.
   - Reads top-level **files only** (`fs.readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true })`, `entry.isFile()`), excluding `task.md`; captures `mtimeMs`/`mtime` via `fs.statSync`; returns `[{ filename, path: './<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>', mtimeMs }]` sorted **newest first** (mtime desc, filename asc tiebreak).
   - Missing/unreadable dir → `{ files: [], dirExists: false }` (never throws), mirroring `listTaskImages` in `api/work/taskAssets.js`.
   - Traversal safety like `taskAssetDir`: reject when the resolved folder's basename isn't the taskId.
   - Repo gate: `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` allows only ONE top-level `function` declaration per **new** file (arrow-function constants are exempt). Either split helpers into one file each or use `export const fn = (...) => {}` style; do not add to the allowlist.

+ *   source for the `# Previous Reports` prompt section. `task.md` (the
+ *   task's own metadata file) and subdirectories are excluded; every other
+ *   extension is included, including links that resolve to a regular file.

+ *   is rejected the same way; an entry that cannot be stat'ed (deleted
+ *   mid-read, broken link) is omitted rather than listed with a zero time,
+ *   so the prompt never names a file the agent cannot open. Never throws.
+ * @example listTaskDocsFiles('/repo', 'task-1').files => [{ filename: 'SURVEY.md', path: './docs/tasks/task-1/SURVEY.md', mtimeMs: 123 }]
+ * @param {string} projectCwd - Absolute project working directory.
+ * @param {string} taskId - Task id (also the folder's final segment).
+ * @param {Object|string} [docsProject] - Project record (or bare folder name) carrying `docsDirName`.
+ * @returns {{files: Array<{filename: string, path: string, mtimeMs: number}>, dirExists: boolean, docsDirName: string}}
+ ***/
+export const listTaskDocsFiles = (projectCwd, taskId, docsProject) => {
+	const docsProjectRecord =
+		typeof docsProject === "string" ? { docsDirName: docsProject } : docsProject;
+	const docsDirName = resolveDocsDirName(docsProjectRecord);
+	if (!projectCwd || !taskId || typeof taskId !== "string") {
+		return { files: [], dirExists: false, docsDirName };
+	}
+	const taskDocsDir = resolveTaskDocsDir(projectCwd, docsProjectRecord, taskId);
+	const tasksRoot = resolveTasksDir(projectCwd, docsProjectRecord);
+	if (
+		!taskDocsDir ||
+		!tasksRoot ||
+		path.basename(taskDocsDir) !== taskId ||

Read text file `docs/KB Code Standards.md`.
1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|  
19|  
20|
21|## Functional over Object oreintated
22|
23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
24|
25|### Principles
26|
27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
34|
35|
36|## Co-location over abstraction
37|
38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
39|
40|### Principles
41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
46|- Don’t fear repetition of code
47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
48|- Use folders as a tool for organising
49|
50|## Tested over trusted 
51|
52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
53|
54|### Principles
55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
58|- Tests must be consistent
59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
61|
62|
63|## Fast iteration over long planning
64|
65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
66|
67|### Principles
68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
74|
75|
76|
77|# Inspirations
78|My principles here are inspired by:
79|
80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
81|- Life isn’t binary (book)
82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
83|
84|
85|# Examples
86|
87|## Intent Driven descriptions
88|
89|### Bad Example
90|
91|```js
92|
93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
94|
95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
96|
97|    users.push(user)
98|  
99|}
100|
101|const list = []
102|
103|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
104|
105|
106|```
107|
108|## Good example
109|
110|```js
111|
112|/**
113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
117|*/
118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
120|  
121|  return ageNextYear
122|}
123|
124|const userObjectsList = []
125|
126|const usersName = "Frank"
127|const usersAge = 32
128|
129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
130|
131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
132|
133|
134|```

1|# Values
2|
3|## User understandable over technical language
4|
5|I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible
6|
7|### Principles
8|
9|- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
10|- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
11|- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
12|- File structure should reflect the call stack
13|- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
14|- Include why things are done not just what is done
15|- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
16|- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
17|- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
18|  
19|  
20|
21|## Functional over Object oreintated
22|
23|Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).
24|
25|### Principles
26|
27|- Try and avoid using classes where possible
28|- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
29|- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
30|- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
31|- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
32|- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
33|- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility
34|
35|
36|## Co-location over abstraction
37|
38|Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.
39|
40|### Principles
41|- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
42|- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
43|- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
44|- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
45|- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
46|- Don’t fear repetition of code
47|- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
48|- Use folders as a tool for organising
49|
50|## Tested over trusted 
51|
52|Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 
53|
54|### Principles
55|- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
56|- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
57|- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
58|- Tests must be consistent
59|- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
60|- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle
61|
62|
63|## Fast iteration over long planning
64|
65|Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.
66|
67|### Principles
68|- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
69|- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
70|- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
71|- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
72|- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
73|- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.
74|
75|
76|
77|# Inspirations
78|My principles here are inspired by:
79|
80|- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
81|- Life isn’t binary (book)
82|- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)
83|
84|
85|# Examples
86|
87|## Intent Driven descriptions
88|
89|### Bad Example
90|
91|```js
92|
93|const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {
94|
95|    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}
96|
97|    users.push(user)
98|  
99|}
100|
101|const list = []
102|
103|userFactory("Frank",32,list)
104|
105|
106|```
107|
108|## Good example
109|
110|```js
111|
112|/**
113|* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
114|* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
115|* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
116|console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
117|*/
118|const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
119|  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
120|  
121|  return ageNextYear
122|}
123|
124|const userObjectsList = []
125|
126|const usersName = "Frank"
127|const usersAge = 32
128|
129|const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})
130|
131|userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})
132|
133|
134|```

Read text file `docs/tasks/4f927ecb-ba3a-423c-ace3-5f7dd7d36896/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — Disk-authoritative "Previous Reports" in stage prompts
2|
3|**Task:** 4f927ecb-ba3a-423c-ace3-5f7dd7d36896
4|**Problem:** Stage prompts render a `# Previous Reports` list from task/history metadata (`task.reports`) without checking the filesystem, so stages name files that do not exist under `docs/tasks/<taskId>/`. Agents waste effort reading phantom files (case study: task `0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5`, whose retrospective prompt listed `idea-20261115-222653.md`, `review-plan-20261115-223714.md`, `automated-tests-failure-20261115-233558.md`, `final-review-20261116-064824.md` — none on disk; flagged in `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/stage-review-20261116.md`).
5|
6|**Fix (one sentence):** When rendering the Previous Reports list, enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` and list only those — never stale, planned, or templated filenames.
7|
8|**Acceptance criteria:**
9|1. For any task, every file named in `# Previous Reports` opens successfully from the workspace.
10|2. No manually-created file on disk in the task docs folder is omitted from the listing (accounted for either by name or by an explicit overflow count + folder pointer — see survey q2 note).
11|
12|---
13|
14|## 1. Survey decisions to encode (from SURVEY.md, round 1)
15|
16|| Q | Decision | Requirement |
17||---|----------|-------------|
18|| q1 | "Leave it out completely" | A report referenced by history but missing on disk is **omitted** from the prompt list (no `MISSING` label in the prompt). |
19|| q2 | "Every file in the folder, including pictures", note: cap to ~top 5 most recently edited, then a guide to view the rest | Enumerate **all top-level files** in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` (any extension, not just `.md`; `task.md` itself excluded), newest first, capped at `N` (default 5) with an overflow line pointing at the folder. |
20|| q3 | "Newest first" | Sort by file mtime, descending (filename tiebreak). |
21|| q4 | "Keep the section but say that no reports are available yet" | Empty/missing task folder → the section still renders, with an explicit "no previous reports available yet" line. |
22|| q5 | "Every stage prompt of every task, always" | The rule lives at the single render choke point in `curatePrompt` / `interpolatePromptKeywords`, so all callers get it uniformly. |
23|
24|The task statement allows "omit or mark MISSING"; the survey chose **omit** — implement omit.
25|
26|---
27|
28|## 2. Root cause (research findings)
29|
30|The prompt list is rendered from **metadata only**, never reconciled with disk:
31|
32|- `api/promptCuration.js:883-895` (`curatePrompt`, section 3) builds `# Previous Reports` from `options.previousReports || options.reports || task.reports` (`api/promptCuration.js:760-776`) and prints each entry verbatim.
33|- `api/promptCuration.js:348-358` (`interpolatePromptKeywords`, `{{previousReports}}`) merges `reports` + `latestReports` + `task.reports` — same phantom source. This keyword also feeds `KAINBAIN_REPORTS` for command stages (`api/flow/commandStages.js:526`), and `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` (`api/promptCuration.js:380-437`) derive from the same merged list.
34|- `task.reports` accumulates entries in `saveStageReport` (`api/watch/stageReports.js:247-257`) and in `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593-667`), which merges in-memory metadata with on-disk `.md` files but **never drops metadata entries whose file is gone** — phantom entries persist forever and flow into prompts.
35|- Callers that pass the list: `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js:693` (`store.getTaskReports(...)` → `reports` option), `api/flow/curateRunnerPrompt.js:48` (`task.reports`), plus the `task.reports` fallback for `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js:249,323` and `api/flow/taskFlowRoutes.js:60`.
36|
37|Verified against the case study: `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/` contains only `SURVEY.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md`, three verdict/review `.md` files and three `.png`s — the four files named in the retrospective prompt do not exist.
38|
39|---
40|
41|## 3. Design (make the change easy, then make the change)
42|
43|**Principle:** one disk-authoritative choke point at render time, so every caller and every task gets the fix without touching dispatch code.
44|
45|1. **New enumerator** `listTaskDocsFiles(projectCwd, taskId, docsProject)` in a new module under `api/work/` (e.g. `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`):
46|   - Resolves the task docs dir via the existing `resolveTaskDocsDir(projectCwd, docsProject, taskId)` (`api/docsPath.js`) so custom `docsDirName` projects work.
47|   - Reads top-level **files only** (`fs.readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true })`, `entry.isFile()`), excluding `task.md`; captures `mtimeMs`/`mtime` via `fs.statSync`; returns `[{ filename, path: './<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>', mtimeMs }]` sorted **newest first** (mtime desc, filename asc tiebreak).
48|   - Missing/unreadable dir → `{ files: [], dirExists: false }` (never throws), mirroring `listTaskImages` in `api/work/taskAssets.js`.
49|   - Traversal safety like `taskAssetDir`: reject when the resolved folder's basename isn't the taskId.
50|   - Repo gate: `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` allows only ONE top-level `function` declaration per **new** file (arrow-function constants are exempt). Either split helpers into one file each or use `export const fn = (...) => {}` style; do not add to the allowlist.
51|   - eslint `security/detect-non-literal-fs-filename`: wrap fs calls in the same `eslint-disable/enable` pair used in `taskAssets.js`/`taskPersistence.js`.
52|
53|2. **Render-time reconciliation in `api/promptCuration.js`** (the file is allowlisted for multiple functions):
54|   - Section 3 (`curatePrompt`, ~line 883): when `projectCwd` (from `interpolationContext`) and `task.id` are present, call `listTaskDocsFiles` and build the section **from disk files only**:
55|     - Header: `# Previous Reports` + "The following files are present in `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/`:" (wording updated from "prior stage reports are available" since the list now includes every file, per q2).
56|     - One `- ./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>` line per file, newest first, capped at `appConfig.taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` (new, default 5), plus overflow line `- (+N more files not listed; list ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ to see them)` (mirrors `formatImageRefs`' cap+overflow pattern at `api/promptCuration.js:76-108`).
57|     - Empty/missing dir → `# Previous Reports\nNo previous reports are available yet — the task folder ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ contains no files.` (q4).
58|     - When `projectCwd` is absent (pure preview, e.g. `api/routes/promptLayout.js` sample which passes no cwd): keep the **legacy** passthrough of the passed-in list byte-identical, so preview routes and no-cwd layouts are unaffected.
59|   - `interpolatePromptKeywords` (`{{previousReports}}`, ~line 348; also feed `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}`): when `projectCwd` + `task.id` resolve, replace the merged `allReports` with the disk enumeration merged with metadata (match by `filename`) so content/slug for `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` still works for real files; phantom metadata entries are dropped (q1). The keyword lists **all** on-disk files newest-first (no cap — it is machine-consumed, e.g. `KAINBAIN_REPORTS`), each as a `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<file>` path; empty → keep the existing `(No previous stage reports available)` fallback. When no `projectCwd`: legacy behaviour unchanged.
60|   - `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593`): **non-destructive** hardening — when the task docs dir is readable, set `missingOnDisk: true` on metadata entries whose filename is absent (kept in `task.reports` because reliability/observability readers — `api/watch/reliabilityShared.js`, `harnessReliability.js`, `aliasReliability.js`, `observabilityMetrics.js` — consume metadata, not files). Do NOT delete entries. The prompt never reads this flag (it enumerates disk directly); it is there so API/UI consumers can later show/omit missing entries.
61|
62|3. **New config knob** `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` in `api/config/schema.js`, mirroring `taskImageMaxPromptRefs` (schema.js:1742): `env: "KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS"`, `type: "int"`, `default: 5`, `min: 0`, `group: "tasks"`, doc: "Max task-folder files listed in one curated stage prompt's # Previous Reports section (newest first; overflow is summarized). 0 = list all." Update the defaults snapshot in `api/config/config.test.js` (~line 185) and the env docs (`site-docs/ports-env.md`; enforced by `api/config/docs.envCoverage.test.js` / `scripts/generate-env-example.mjs`).
63|
64|4. **Descriptor text updates** (semantics changed): `shared/promptLayout.js` `LAYOUT_TOKENS` entry for `previousReports` (~line 133), `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js` hint for `{{previousReports}}` (~line 68), and the JSDoc for `{{previousReports}}` in `api/promptCuration.js:116` — all should say "files actually present in the task docs folder, newest first".
65|
66|**Why render-time and not in `getTaskReports`:** the prompt must enumerate disk directly (the requirement), and `task.reports` is shared with reliability analytics that legitimately keep metadata-only entries. Keeping the fix in `curatePrompt`/`interpolatePromptKeywords` covers all five call sites at once (q5) with no dispatch-code changes.
67|
68|---
69|
70|## 4. Step-by-step implementation order
71|
72|1. **Config + enumerator (foundation first):** add `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` to `api/config/schema.js`; create `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js` with `listTaskDocsFiles` (+ per-file split if the one-function gate requires); unit-test the enumerator alone (`api/work/taskDocsFiles.test.js`): tmp dir with mixed files (`.md`, `.png`, `task.md`, a subdir), mtime ordering, custom `docsDirName`, missing dir, traversal rejection.
73|2. **Render choke point:** change section 3 in `curatePrompt` and the `{{previousReports}}`/`{{latestReportPath}}`/`{{latestReport:<slug>}}` branches in `interpolatePromptKeywords` per §3.2. Add a `formatPreviousReportsSection(diskFiles, { maxRefs, docsDirName, taskId })` builder next to `formatImageRefs` so section text is testable in isolation.
74|3. **Non-destructive marking:** `syncTaskReports` sets `missingOnDisk` on metadata entries absent from a readable dir.
75|4. **Descriptors:** update `shared/promptLayout.js`, `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js`, JSDoc in `api/promptCuration.js`.
76|5. **Tests** (see §5).
77|6. **Docs** (see §6).
78|7. **Full gates** (see §7).
79|
80|---
81|
82|## 5. Testing plan
83|
84|Primary gate: `npm run test:api` (vitest) — run touched suites first, then `npm run test:unit`; lint via `npm run lint:api`.
85|
86|**New tests:**
87|- `api/work/taskDocsFiles.test.js` — enumerator behaviour (see step 1).
88|- `api/promptCuration.diskReports.test.js` (new file; promptCuration.test.js is huge) — with a **real tmp project dir**:
89|  - phantom entries in `options.previousReports`/`task.reports` are omitted from `# Previous Reports`; only on-disk files are listed;
90|  - manually created file (e.g. `MY_NOTES.md`) on disk with no metadata **is** listed (acceptance 2);
91|  - newest-first ordering by mtime; non-`.md` files (png) included; `task.md` excluded;
92|  - cap: with 7 files and cap 5, exactly 5 listed + overflow line with `(+2 more`;
93|  - empty dir / missing dir → section renders with the "no previous reports available yet" line (q4);
94|  - no `projectCwd` → legacy passthrough of the passed list (byte-identical to today);
95|  - custom `docsDirName` project → enumerates `<cwd>/kainbain-docs/tasks/<id>/` and lists `./kainbain-docs/...` paths;
96|  - `{{previousReports}}` keyword with real dir → all on-disk files newest-first, phantoms dropped; `{{latestReportPath}}` never returns a phantom; `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` returns content only for on-disk reports;
97|  - **case-study regression fixture**: replicate task `0d29c64c...` — metadata lists `idea-20261115-222653.md`, `review-plan-20261115-223714.md`, `automated-tests-failure-20261115-233558.md`, `final-review-20261116-064824.md`; disk has `SURVEY.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md`, 3 verdict files + pngs → assert none of the four phantoms appears in the prompt and every listed path exists on disk (acceptance 1, executable form).
98|- `api/taskStore.test.js` (extend near existing `getTaskReports` tests ~lines 431/1248/1618): `syncTaskReports` marks `missingOnDisk` on phantom metadata entries when the dir is readable, keeps metadata-only entries intact when the dir is absent (test-env fallback), and still picks up manually created `.md` files.

102|- `api/promptCuration.test.js:151-166` ("includes previous reports section…") — passes no `projectCwd`, so legacy path keeps it green; add a cwd variant. 136|## 8. Risks and edge cases
137|
138|- **Fake cwds in tests** (`/projects/demo`, `/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain`): with a cwd set, rendering becomes disk-authoritative, so these fixtures must move to tmp dirs — handled in §5.
139|- **Custom `docsDirName`** projects: enumerator uses `resolveTaskDocsDir`, covered by a test.
140|- **Runner worktree retargeting:** curation happens backend-side with the backend `projectCwd`; the runner only rewrites the path prefix in the finished string, so relative `./docs/tasks/<id>/...` entries stay valid. No runner change needed.
141|- **Empty/missing task folder** (brand-new task): renders the "no previous reports available yet" line (q4) instead of omitting the section silently.
142|- **`task.md` exclusion:** the task's own metadata file must never be listed as a report.
143|- **Subdirectories (e.g. `assets/`):** only top-level files are listed; images under `assets/` remain covered by the separate `# Task Images` section (`collectTaskImageRefs`). Top-level pngs (like the case study's) are listed per survey q2.
144|- **Reliability analytics:** `task.reports` metadata is intentionally preserved (only flagged `missingOnDisk`), so `harnessReliability`/`aliasReliability`/`observabilityMetrics` are unaffected.
145|- **Cap vs. "no on-disk report omitted":** the survey (q2 note) explicitly caps the list at ~5 newest with a pointer line; the overflow line keeps every remaining file discoverable, satisfying acceptance 2. Setting `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS=0` lists all files if a strict reading is ever required.
146|- **Performance:** one `readdirSync` + per-file `statSync` per prompt curation — same cost profile as the existing `collectTaskImageRefs` call in the same function; negligible.

Read text file `docs/tasks/4f927ecb-ba3a-423c-ace3-5f7dd7d36896/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`.
1|# Implementation Plan — Disk-authoritative "Previous Reports" in stage prompts
2|
3|**Task:** 4f927ecb-ba3a-423c-ace3-5f7dd7d36896
4|**Problem:** Stage prompts render a `# Previous Reports` list from task/history metadata (`task.reports`) without checking the filesystem, so stages name files that do not exist under `docs/tasks/<taskId>/`. Agents waste effort reading phantom files (case study: task `0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5`, whose retrospective prompt listed `idea-20261115-222653.md`, `review-plan-20261115-223714.md`, `automated-tests-failure-20261115-233558.md`, `final-review-20261116-064824.md` — none on disk; flagged in `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/stage-review-20261116.md`).
5|
6|**Fix (one sentence):** When rendering the Previous Reports list, enumerate the files actually present in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` and list only those — never stale, planned, or templated filenames.
7|
8|**Acceptance criteria:**
9|1. For any task, every file named in `# Previous Reports` opens successfully from the workspace.
10|2. No manually-created file on disk in the task docs folder is omitted from the listing (accounted for either by name or by an explicit overflow count + folder pointer — see survey q2 note).
11|
12|---
13|
14|## 1. Survey decisions to encode (from SURVEY.md, round 1)
15|
16|| Q | Decision | Requirement |
17||---|----------|-------------|
18|| q1 | "Leave it out completely" | A report referenced by history but missing on disk is **omitted** from the prompt list (no `MISSING` label in the prompt). |
19|| q2 | "Every file in the folder, including pictures", note: cap to ~top 5 most recently edited, then a guide to view the rest | Enumerate **all top-level files** in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` (any extension, not just `.md`; `task.md` itself excluded), newest first, capped at `N` (default 5) with an overflow line pointing at the folder. |
20|| q3 | "Newest first" | Sort by file mtime, descending (filename tiebreak). |
21|| q4 | "Keep the section but say that no reports are available yet" | Empty/missing task folder → the section still renders, with an explicit "no previous reports available yet" line. |
22|| q5 | "Every stage prompt of every task, always" | The rule lives at the single render choke point in `curatePrompt` / `interpolatePromptKeywords`, so all callers get it uniformly. |
23|
24|The task statement allows "omit or mark MISSING"; the survey chose **omit** — implement omit.
25|
26|---
27|
28|## 2. Root cause (research findings)
29|
30|The prompt list is rendered from **metadata only**, never reconciled with disk:
31|
32|- `api/promptCuration.js:883-895` (`curatePrompt`, section 3) builds `# Previous Reports` from `options.previousReports || options.reports || task.reports` (`api/promptCuration.js:760-776`) and prints each entry verbatim.
33|- `api/promptCuration.js:348-358` (`interpolatePromptKeywords`, `{{previousReports}}`) merges `reports` + `latestReports` + `task.reports` — same phantom source. This keyword also feeds `KAINBAIN_REPORTS` for command stages (`api/flow/commandStages.js:526`), and `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` (`api/promptCuration.js:380-437`) derive from the same merged list.
34|- `task.reports` accumulates entries in `saveStageReport` (`api/watch/stageReports.js:247-257`) and in `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593-667`), which merges in-memory metadata with on-disk `.md` files but **never drops metadata entries whose file is gone** — phantom entries persist forever and flow into prompts.
35|- Callers that pass the list: `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js:693` (`store.getTaskReports(...)` → `reports` option), `api/flow/curateRunnerPrompt.js:48` (`task.reports`), plus the `task.reports` fallback for `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js:249,323` and `api/flow/taskFlowRoutes.js:60`.
36|
37|Verified against the case study: `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/` contains only `SURVEY.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md`, three verdict/review `.md` files and three `.png`s — the four files named in the retrospective prompt do not exist.
38|
39|---
40|
41|## 3. Design (make the change easy, then make the change)
42|
43|**Principle:** one disk-authoritative choke point at render time, so every caller and every task gets the fix without touching dispatch code.
44|
45|1. **New enumerator** `listTaskDocsFiles(projectCwd, taskId, docsProject)` in a new module under `api/work/` (e.g. `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`):
46|   - Resolves the task docs dir via the existing `resolveTaskDocsDir(projectCwd, docsProject, taskId)` (`api/docsPath.js`) so custom `docsDirName` projects work.
47|   - Reads top-level **files only** (`fs.readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true })`, `entry.isFile()`), excluding `task.md`; captures `mtimeMs`/`mtime` via `fs.statSync`; returns `[{ filename, path: './<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>', mtimeMs }]` sorted **newest first** (mtime desc, filename asc tiebreak).
48|   - Missing/unreadable dir → `{ files: [], dirExists: false }` (never throws), mirroring `listTaskImages` in `api/work/taskAssets.js`.
49|   - Traversal safety like `taskAssetDir`: reject when the resolved folder's basename isn't the taskId.
50|   - Repo gate: `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` allows only ONE top-level `function` declaration per **new** file (arrow-function constants are exempt). Either split helpers into one file each or use `export const fn = (...) => {}` style; do not add to the allowlist.
51|   - eslint `security/detect-non-literal-fs-filename`: wrap fs calls in the same `eslint-disable/enable` pair used in `taskAssets.js`/`taskPersistence.js`.
52|
53|2. **Render-time reconciliation in `api/promptCuration.js`** (the file is allowlisted for multiple functions):
54|   - Section 3 (`curatePrompt`, ~line 883): when `projectCwd` (from `interpolationContext`) and `task.id` are present, call `listTaskDocsFiles` and build the section **from disk files only**:
55|     - Header: `# Previous Reports` + "The following files are present in `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/`:" (wording updated from "prior stage reports are available" since the list now includes every file, per q2).
56|     - One `- ./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>` line per file, newest first, capped at `appConfig.taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` (new, default 5), plus overflow line `- (+N more files not listed; list ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ to see them)` (mirrors `formatImageRefs`' cap+overflow pattern at `api/promptCuration.js:76-108`).
57|     - Empty/missing dir → `# Previous Reports\nNo previous reports are available yet — the task folder ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ contains no files.` (q4).
58|     - When `projectCwd` is absent (pure preview, e.g. `api/routes/promptLayout.js` sample which passes no cwd): keep the **legacy** passthrough of the passed-in list byte-identical, so preview routes and no-cwd layouts are unaffected.
59|   - `interpolatePromptKeywords` (`{{previousReports}}`, ~line 348; also feed `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}`): when `projectCwd` + `task.id` resolve, replace the merged `allReports` with the disk enumeration merged with metadata (match by `filename`) so content/slug for `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` still works for real files; phantom metadata entries are dropped (q1). The keyword lists **all** on-disk files newest-first (no cap — it is machine-consumed, e.g. `KAINBAIN_REPORTS`), each as a `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<file>` path; empty → keep the existing `(No previous stage reports available)` fallback. When no `projectCwd`: legacy behaviour unchanged.
60|   - `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593`): **non-destructive** hardening — when the task docs dir is readable, set `missingOnDisk: true` on metadata entries whose filename is absent (kept in `task.reports` because reliability/observability readers — `api/watch/reliabilityShared.js`, `harnessReliability.js`, `aliasReliability.js`, `observabilityMetrics.js` — consume metadata, not files). Do NOT delete entries. The prompt never reads this flag (it enumerates disk directly); it is there so API/UI consumers can later show/omit missing entries.
61|
62|3. **New config knob** `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` in `api/config/schema.js`, mirroring `taskImageMaxPromptRefs` (schema.js:1742): `env: "KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS"`, `type: "int"`, `default: 5`, `min: 0`, `group: "tasks"`, doc: "Max task-folder files listed in one curated stage prompt's # Previous Reports section (newest first; overflow is summarized). 0 = list all." Update the defaults snapshot in `api/config/config.test.js` (~line 185) and the env docs (`site-docs/ports-env.md`; enforced by `api/config/docs.envCoverage.test.js` / `scripts/generate-env-example.mjs`).
63|
64|4. **Descriptor text updates** (semantics changed): `shared/promptLayout.js` `LAYOUT_TOKENS` entry for `previousReports` (~line 133), `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js` hint for `{{previousReports}}` (~line 68), and the JSDoc for `{{previousReports}}` in `api/promptCuration.js:116` — all should say "files actually present in the task docs folder, newest first".
65|
66|**Why render-time and not in `getTaskReports`:** the prompt must enumerate disk directly (the requirement), and `task.reports` is shared with reliability analytics that legitimately keep metadata-only entries. Keeping the fix in `curatePrompt`/`interpolatePromptKeywords` covers all five call sites at once (q5) with no dispatch-code changes.
67|
68|---
69|
70|## 4. Step-by-step implementation order
71|
72|1. **Config + enumerator (foundation first):** add `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` to `api/config/schema.js`; create `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js` with `listTaskDocsFiles` (+ per-file split if the one-function gate requires); unit-test the enumerator alone (`api/work/taskDocsFiles.test.js`): tmp dir with mixed files (`.md`, `.png`, `task.md`, a subdir), mtime ordering, custom `docsDirName`, missing dir, traversal rejection.
73|2. **Render choke point:** change section 3 in `curatePrompt` and the `{{previousReports}}`/`{{latestReportPath}}`/`{{latestReport:<slug>}}` branches in `interpolatePromptKeywords` per §3.2. Add a `formatPreviousReportsSection(diskFiles, { maxRefs, docsDirName, taskId })` builder next to `formatImageRefs` so section text is testable in isolation.
74|3. **Non-destructive marking:** `syncTaskReports` sets `missingOnDisk` on metadata entries absent from a readable dir.
75|4. **Descriptors:** update `shared/promptLayout.js`, `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js`, JSDoc in `api/promptCuration.js`.
76|5. **Tests** (see §5).

136|## 8. Risks and edge cases
137|
138|- **Fake cwds in tests** (`/projects/demo`, `/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain`): with a cwd set, rendering becomes disk-authoritative, so these fixtures must move to tmp dirs — handled in §5.
139|- **Custom `docsDirName`** projects: enumerator uses `resolveTaskDocsDir`, covered by a test.
140|- **Runner worktree retargeting:** curation happens backend-side with the backend `projectCwd`; the runner only rewrites the path prefix in the finished string, so relative `./docs/tasks/<id>/...` entries stay valid. No runner change needed.
141|- **Empty/missing task folder** (brand-new task): renders the "no previous reports available yet" line (q4) instead of omitting the section silently.
142|- **`task.md` exclusion:** the task's own metadata file must never be listed as a report.
143|- **Subdirectories (e.g. `assets/`):** only top-level files are listed; images under `assets/` remain covered by the separate `# Task Images` section (`collectTaskImageRefs`). Top-level pngs (like the case study's) are listed per survey q2.
144|- **Reliability analytics:** `task.reports` metadata is intentionally preserved (only flagged `missingOnDisk`), so `harnessReliability`/`aliasReliability`/`observabilityMetrics` are unaffected.
145|- **Cap vs. "no on-disk report omitted":** the survey (q2 note) explicitly caps the list at ~5 newest with a pointer line; the overflow line keeps every remaining file discoverable, satisfying acceptance 2. Setting `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS=0` lists all files if a strict reading is ever required.
146|- **Performance:** one `readdirSync` + per-file `statSync` per prompt curation — same cost profile as the existing `collectTaskImageRefs` call in the same function; negligible.

+Agent/review stages never share a session. Every stage execution begins a brand-new agent session whose only context is that stage's curated prompt: the task goal, the stage instructions, references to prior stages' report artifacts, and any failure/steering guidance. 12|---
13|
14|## 1. Survey decisions to encode (from SURVEY.md, round 1)
15|
16|| Q | Decision | Requirement |
17||---|----------|-------------|
18|| q1 | "Leave it out completely" | A report referenced by history but missing on disk is **omitted** from the prompt list (no `MISSING` label in the prompt). |
19|| q2 | "Every file in the folder, including pictures", note: cap to ~top 5 most recently edited, then a guide to view the rest | Enumerate **all top-level files** in `docs/tasks/<taskId>/` (any extension, not just `.md`; `task.md` itself excluded), newest first, capped at `N` (default 5) with an overflow line pointing at the folder. |
20|| q3 | "Newest first" | Sort by file mtime, descending (filename tiebreak). |
21|| q4 | "Keep the section but say that no reports are available yet" | Empty/missing task folder → the section still renders, with an explicit "no previous reports available yet" line. |
22|| q5 | "Every stage prompt of every task, always" | The rule lives at the single render choke point in `curatePrompt` / `interpolatePromptKeywords`, so all callers get it uniformly. |
23|
24|The task statement allows "omit or mark MISSING"; the survey chose **omit** — implement omit.
25|
26|---
27|
28|## 2. Root cause (research findings)
29|
30|The prompt list is rendered from **metadata only**, never reconciled with disk:
31|
32|- `api/promptCuration.js:883-895` (`curatePrompt`, section 3) builds `# Previous Reports` from `options.previousReports || options.reports || task.reports` (`api/promptCuration.js:760-776`) and prints each entry verbatim.
33|- `api/promptCuration.js:348-358` (`interpolatePromptKeywords`, `{{previousReports}}`) merges `reports` + `latestReports` + `task.reports` — same phantom source. This keyword also feeds `KAINBAIN_REPORTS` for command stages (`api/flow/commandStages.js:526`), and `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` (`api/promptCuration.js:380-437`) derive from the same merged list.
34|- `task.reports` accumulates entries in `saveStageReport` (`api/watch/stageReports.js:247-257`) and in `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593-667`), which merges in-memory metadata with on-disk `.md` files but **never drops metadata entries whose file is gone** — phantom entries persist forever and flow into prompts.
35|- Callers that pass the list: `api/flow/execution/executeStage.js:693` (`store.getTaskReports(...)` → `reports` option), `api/flow/curateRunnerPrompt.js:48` (`task.reports`), plus the `task.reports` fallback for `api/work/taskWorkRoutes.js:249,323` and `api/flow/taskFlowRoutes.js:60`.
36|
37|Verified against the case study: `docs/tasks/0d29c64c-34f5-4740-ba25-f4e6ef4f90b5/` contains only `SURVEY.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, `OVERFLOW_FIX_NOTE.md`, three verdict/review `.md` files and three `.png`s — the four files named in the retrospective prompt do not exist.
38|
39|---
40|
41|## 3. Design (make the change easy, then make the change)
42|
43|**Principle:** one disk-authoritative choke point at render time, so every caller and every task gets the fix without touching dispatch code.
44|
45|1. **New enumerator** `listTaskDocsFiles(projectCwd, taskId, docsProject)` in a new module under `api/work/` (e.g. `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js`):
46|   - Resolves the task docs dir via the existing `resolveTaskDocsDir(projectCwd, docsProject, taskId)` (`api/docsPath.js`) so custom `docsDirName` projects work.
47|   - Reads top-level **files only** (`fs.readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true })`, `entry.isFile()`), excluding `task.md`; captures `mtimeMs`/`mtime` via `fs.statSync`; returns `[{ filename, path: './<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>', mtimeMs }]` sorted **newest first** (mtime desc, filename asc tiebreak).
48|   - Missing/unreadable dir → `{ files: [], dirExists: false }` (never throws), mirroring `listTaskImages` in `api/work/taskAssets.js`.
49|   - Traversal safety like `taskAssetDir`: reject when the resolved folder's basename isn't the taskId.
50|   - Repo gate: `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs` allows only ONE top-level `function` declaration per **new** file (arrow-function constants are exempt). Either split helpers into one file each or use `export const fn = (...) => {}` style; do not add to the allowlist.
51|   - eslint `security/detect-non-literal-fs-filename`: wrap fs calls in the same `eslint-disable/enable` pair used in `taskAssets.js`/`taskPersistence.js`.
52|
53|2. **Render-time reconciliation in `api/promptCuration.js`** (the file is allowlisted for multiple functions):
54|   - Section 3 (`curatePrompt`, ~line 883): when `projectCwd` (from `interpolationContext`) and `task.id` are present, call `listTaskDocsFiles` and build the section **from disk files only**:
55|     - Header: `# Previous Reports` + "The following files are present in `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/`:" (wording updated from "prior stage reports are available" since the list now includes every file, per q2).
56|     - One `- ./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<filename>` line per file, newest first, capped at `appConfig.taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` (new, default 5), plus overflow line `- (+N more files not listed; list ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ to see them)` (mirrors `formatImageRefs`' cap+overflow pattern at `api/promptCuration.js:76-108`).
57|     - Empty/missing dir → `# Previous Reports\nNo previous reports are available yet — the task folder ./.<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/ contains no files.` (q4).
58|     - When `projectCwd` is absent (pure preview, e.g. `api/routes/promptLayout.js` sample which passes no cwd): keep the **legacy** passthrough of the passed-in list byte-identical, so preview routes and no-cwd layouts are unaffected.
59|   - `interpolatePromptKeywords` (`{{previousReports}}`, ~line 348; also feed `{{latestReportPath}}` / `{{latestReport:<slug>}}`): when `projectCwd` + `task.id` resolve, replace the merged `allReports` with the disk enumeration merged with metadata (match by `filename`) so content/slug for `{{latestReport:<slug>}}` still works for real files; phantom metadata entries are dropped (q1). The keyword lists **all** on-disk files newest-first (no cap — it is machine-consumed, e.g. `KAINBAIN_REPORTS`), each as a `./<docsDirName>/tasks/<taskId>/<file>` path; empty → keep the existing `(No previous stage reports available)` fallback. When no `projectCwd`: legacy behaviour unchanged.
60|   - `syncTaskReports` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:593`): **non-destructive** hardening — when the task docs dir is readable, set `missingOnDisk: true` on metadata entries whose filename is absent (kept in `task.reports` because reliability/observability readers — `api/watch/reliabilityShared.js`, `harnessReliability.js`, `aliasReliability.js`, `observabilityMetrics.js` — consume metadata, not files). Do NOT delete entries. The prompt never reads this flag (it enumerates disk directly); it is there so API/UI consumers can later show/omit missing entries.
61|
62|3. **New config knob** `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` in `api/config/schema.js`, mirroring `taskImageMaxPromptRefs` (schema.js:1742): `env: "KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS"`, `type: "int"`, `default: 5`, `min: 0`, `group: "tasks"`, doc: "Max task-folder files listed in one curated stage prompt's # Previous Reports section (newest first; overflow is summarized). 0 = list all." Update the defaults snapshot in `api/config/config.test.js` (~line 185) and the env docs (`site-docs/ports-env.md`; enforced by `api/config/docs.envCoverage.test.js` / `scripts/generate-env-example.mjs`).
63|
64|4. **Descriptor text updates** (semantics changed): `shared/promptLayout.js` `LAYOUT_TOKENS` entry for `previousReports` (~line 133), `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js` hint for `{{previousReports}}` (~line 68), and the JSDoc for `{{previousReports}}` in `api/promptCuration.js:116` — all should say "files actually present in the task docs folder, newest first".
65|
66|**Why render-time and not in `getTaskReports`:** the prompt must enumerate disk directly (the requirement), and `task.reports` is shared with reliability analytics that legitimately keep metadata-only entries. Keeping the fix in `curatePrompt`/`interpolatePromptKeywords` covers all five call sites at once (q5) with no dispatch-code changes.
67|
68|---
69|
70|## 4. Step-by-step implementation order
71|
72|1. **Config + enumerator (foundation first):** add `taskReportsMaxPromptRefs` to `api/config/schema.js`; create `api/work/taskDocsFiles.js` with `listTaskDocsFiles` (+ per-file split if the one-function gate requires); unit-test the enumerator alone (`api/work/taskDocsFiles.test.js`): tmp dir with mixed files (`.md`, `.png`, `task.md`, a subdir), mtime ordering, custom `docsDirName`, missing dir, traversal rejection.
73|2. **Render choke point:** change section 3 in `curatePrompt` and the `{{previousReports}}`/`{{latestReportPath}}`/`{{latestReport:<slug>}}` branches in `interpolatePromptKeywords` per §3.2. Add a `formatPreviousReportsSection(diskFiles, { maxRefs, docsDirName, taskId })` builder next to `formatImageRefs` so section text is testable in isolation.
74|3. **Non-destructive marking:** `syncTaskReports` sets `missingOnDisk` on metadata entries absent from a readable dir.
75|4. **Descriptors:** update `shared/promptLayout.js`, `shared/stageKeywordTokens.js`, JSDoc in `api/promptCuration.js`.
76|5. **Tests** (see §5).
77|6. **Docs** (see §6).
78|7. **Full gates** (see §7).

123|## 7. Verification checklist (Definition of Done)
124|
125|- [ ] `npm run test:api` passes (full vitest suite), including all touched suites listed in §5.
126|- [ ] `npm run test:unit` passes (api + frontend).

129|- [ ] `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs` clean after doc edits.
130|- [ ] Executable acceptance: a test (the case-study fixture in §5) proves every `# Previous Reports` entry exists on disk and no on-disk file is silently omitted; run the real-repo check for task `0d29c64c...` described in §5.

136|## 8. Risks and edge cases
137|
138|- **Fake cwds in tests** (`/projects/demo`, `/home/[REDACTED]/projects/kainbain`): with a cwd set, rendering becomes disk-authoritative, so these fixtures must move to tmp dirs — handled in §5.
139|- **Custom `docsDirName`** projects: enumerator uses `resolveTaskDocsDir`, covered by a test.
140|- **Runner worktree retargeting:** curation happens backend-side with the backend `projectCwd`; the runner only rewrites the path prefix in the finished string, so relative `./docs/tasks/<id>/...` entries stay valid. No runner change needed.
141|- **Empty/missing task folder** (brand-new task): renders the "no previous reports available yet" line (q4) instead of omitting the section silently.
142|- **`task.md` exclusion:** the task's own metadata file must never be listed as a report.
143|- **Subdirectories (e.g. `assets/`):** only top-level files are listed; images under `assets/` remain covered by the separate `# Task Images` section (`collectTaskImageRefs`). Top-level pngs (like the case study's) are listed per survey q2.
144|- **Reliability analytics:** `task.reports` metadata is intentionally preserved (only flagged `missingOnDisk`), so `harnessReliability`/`aliasReliability`/`observabilityMetrics` are unaffected.
145|- **Cap vs. "no on-disk report omitted":** the survey (q2 note) explicitly caps the list at ~5 newest with a pointer line; the overflow line keeps every remaining file discoverable, satisfying acceptance 2. Setting `KAINBAIN_TASK_REPORTS_MAX_PROMPT_REFS=0` lists all files if a strict reading is ever required.
146|- **Performance:** one `readdirSync` + per-file `statSync` per prompt curation — same cost profile as the existing `collectTaskImageRefs` call in the same function; negligible.
